AztecProtocol/aztec-packages.name: v4.2.1
AztecProtocol/aztec-packages.body:
Release 4.2.1 is a **MANDATORY** single-fix patch on top of 4.2.0. 

The on-chain check for "has this payload already been proposed?" was timing out at the RPC layer so signaling was suppressed across the validator set. This hotfix release restores governance signaling. 

## Bug Fixes

- **Sequencers could not signal governance payloads on long-lived rollups** ([#23001](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/23001)): The "has this payload already been proposed?" check used `eth_getLogs` over the rollup's full L1 deployment range. Once that range exceeded typical RPC provider block-range caps the call timed out, the publisher treated the timeout as "already proposed," and sequencers silently stopped signaling. 
  
  The publisher now re-checks each slot rather than caching a permanent verdict, and the RPC-failure mode is switched from fail-closed to **fail-open** — a flaky L1 endpoint should not silence governance participation, and a duplicate signal is harmless.
